title: Add NumParser struct to Rust num-parser library
description: Brownfield Rust refactor: wrap the panicking free functions in a NumParser struct with Result-returning methods.

task_spec.prompt:
Add a NumParser struct to src/lib.rs. All 3 existing tests must still pass.

  pub struct NumParser;

  impl NumParser {
      pub fn new() -> Self

      pub fn parse_int(&self, s: &str) -> Result<i32, String>
        — parses s as i32; returns Err(format!("invalid int: '{}'", s)) on failure

      pub fn parse_pair(&self, s: &str) -> Result<(i32, i32), String>
        — splits on first ',' and parses both parts as i32
        — returns Err("expected 'a,b' format".to_string()) if no comma
        — returns Err(format!("invalid int: '{}'", part)) if a part fails to parse

      pub fn parse_and_sum(&self, s: &str) -> Result<i32, String>
        — delegates to parse_pair, returns Ok(a + b)
  }

Do not remove or modify the existing free functions.
All 3 existing tests must still pass.
Run: cargo test
required_artifacts: NumParser::parse_int returns Ok(i32) or Err with message
NumParser::parse_pair returns Ok((i32, i32)) or Err with message
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `cargo test` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
